newsitem.title: USA: FTC staffers may oppose Staples merger - report.
newsitem.headline: FTC staffers may oppose Staples merger - report.

text.p: Federal Trade Commission staffers may recommend this week the full commission move to block the merger of Staples and Office Depot, it was reported Wednesday.

FTC WATCH newsletter said that staffers "have alerted the commissioners to the possibility they will be sending up a recommendation to seek a preliminary injunction" blocking the merger. An FTC spokeswoman had no comment.

At issue in the merger is whether the FTC views Staples and Office Depot as a small part of a huge market for office supplies, computers and office furniture sold in thousands of stores across the country.
In that case the merger would have little effect on competition, except perhaps in the few cities where the two chains compete directly against each other, analysts say.

Alternatively, the FTC could view the merger as narrowing competition from the nation's three office superstore chains -- the third is OfficeMax Inc -- to two. In that case they might see the merger as anticompetitive.
A Staples spokesman has said the FTC pledged to reach a decision by Feb. 25.
Staples and Office Depot have called special shareholder meetings set for Feb. 27 to consider the merger. The two companies announced their plans on Sept. 4, 1996.
A spokeswoman for Staples on Wednesday dismissed the story as "total speculation."

"We don't know anything about it. This is not information that has been shared with us," said Jean Papagni from company headquarters in Westborough, Mass. "As far as we know we are still on track to receive an answer from the FTC on the 25th."
